**SWORD COAST SIDE QUESTS VOLUME 1**

In the hills near the Sword Coast, there lives a gang of ruffians and thieves known as the Flying Drunks. Their leader is a particularly well-known scoundrel by the name of Kragnoroth. For a while, Kragnoroth and his gang has lain low, but not anymore. He is up to his old ways again, stealing, fighting, and being a dirty wretch. Kill Him! Do it for the good people of the Sword Coast and give him justice from the gods. An adventure for 1st-3rd level characters.

**SWORD COAST SIDE QUESTS VOLUME 1**

_THE LAIR OF KRAGNOROTH THE DRUNK_

BY JOSEPH WILLIAMS

**SWORD COAST SIDE QUESTS**

This adventure module is meant to help the DM with providing content to their players. This adventure is intended to run in the Forgotten Realms Setting. but it can be compatible with any campaign setting, published module, or homebrew adventure. Need to get your player characters (PC's) to a higher level before beginning your next adventure? Want a way to get some loot into the hands of your PC's before they start another long quest? Or do you just need a little more filler in the campaign you already have going? Then Sword Coast Side Quests is for you! This adventure module is meant more as a guide than a concrete structure for this quest. The challenges and foes in this module are meant to be challenging to four (4) to six (6) player characters of 1st-3rd level. If you have more or fewer PC's, then you will need to adjust the number of foes and the difficulty of the traps and other challenges.

  

**THE LEGEND OF KRAGNOROTH THE DRUNK**

Kragnoroth the Drunk originally hailed from the city of Luskan. He was a ship member on Ship Suljack, where he served as a pirate. One night, Kragnoroth and a couple of his shipmates undertook an unsanctioned raid on a nobleman's pleasure yacht. The three raiders snuck aboard and swiped a large chest full of gold and jewels. It was so heavy it nearly sank the rowboat they used to get away in the night. After taking such a large prize, Kragnoroth became afraid of retribution, both from the nobleman and his captain, so he and his friends decided to run to the hills and hide out. Along the way, the three bandits found others looking to live life as they are, and began to gather a gang. Going from town to village, drinking and gathering followers, they decided to officially organize and set up a base of operations, from which they can raid the local countryside. The gang became known as the Flying Drunks shortly after locating a nearby cave. There was a waterfall close to the cave, with a nice pool for swimming at the bottom. Kragnoroth's lieutenant, his longtime friend and shipmate, Joffner, came up with an idea for an initiation ritual. To become a part of the Flying Drunks, initiates are tossed off the waterfall into the pool below, where he or she is to swim to the other side while wearing leather armor, a short sword, and a pouch with 100 copper pieces in it.

**ADVENTURE HOOKS**

As DM, it will be your job to usher your PC's into this dungeon, but it will also be your job to make it appear as though the PC's chose to go there willingly. This is the art of good Dungeon Mastering, and in order to do this, here are a few suggested Adventure Hooks you could use. These are, however, only suggestions. Appendix B also offers players a chance to make this adventure much more personal and meaningful to their characters. These background options can also be used in conjunction with Appendix C, which can provide more incentives to take down Kragnoroth the Drunk and his gang.

**ADVENTURE HOOK ENCOUNTER TABLE**

**1d4**

1. 4 Human Bandits, 1 Human Thug

2. 4 Human Bandits, 1 Scout

3. 2 Thugs

4. 2 Scouts

![](data:image/png;base64,)

Symbol of the Flying Drunks

**Local Merchants**

In a nearby town, Kragnoroth the Drunk and his gang have been robbing local stores. The merchants and magistrate in this town are desperate for anyone who can help stop Kragnoroth from destroying their economy. The merchants would also like to see some of their stolen goods returned to them. If the PC's travel to a shop or store of any kind, or if they stop at the local inn or tavern, they may hear about Kragnoroth this way. Give your PC's added incentive by having a local merchant offer a reward for bringing Kragnoroth to justice. Also, if you do not have at least four PC's, you could have the magistrate offer to guide them and help them fight the gang as an NPC.

**The Drowned Initiate**

Recently, a man named Ned Drummond lost a son to the Flying Drunk's initiation ritual. The PC's can meet Ned, who is extremely angry with Kragnoroth and the entire Flying Drunks gang. He wants to see Kragnoroth killed in retribution for his son's death, and will pay handsomely for proof of Kragnoroth's demise.

**The Heist**

Kragnoroth the Drunk is a fugitive from justice from the city of Luskan. Nobody steals on Captain Suljack's watch, at least not without giving him a cut of the profits. The PC's can be offered a job as bounty hunters, either by Captain Suljack, or through an emissary. Alternately, rather than the Captain seeking Kragnoroth's head, it may be the nobleman who was robbed. Maybe he finally figured out what Kragnoroth had done and where he went afterward. This option could work well if the PC's are already working for a member of the upper class.

**Attacked and Robbed**

This is probably the easiest and most direct way to get the player characters to seek out Kragnoroth. Every band of PC's will need to rest, and many will do so at night. You could have members of the Flying Drunks attack and rob the PC's while they are camped along the road. The players can then learn of the nearby hideout, either from a captured bandit, or by the Flying Drunks' symbol on the bandits (such as a ring, a painted shield, or embossed leather armor), and matching it to the symbol displayed outside Kragnoroth the Drunk's lair. This way could also allow the players to learn of the Surface Shaft, another possible entry point into the lair.

**THE ENCOUNTERS**

The encounters listed here correspond to the numbers shown on the grid map. A majority of the encounters are with members of the Flying Drunks gang, but a few are encounters with giant spiders and traps. The stats for the foes and monsters are found in Appendix A of this book. The text found in the yellow boxes in most encounter sections can be read aloud to your players as a descriptive aid. The information given in the encounters section will tell how many of a foe is present, as well as any environmental hazards or hindrances, such as traps and spider webs. The specific position of the foes or hazards are not marked on the map, making their position strictly up to the DM. Most of the encounters will also yield some sort of treasure. Use the Treasure Tables provided to reward the players after defeating a foe.

**Encounter 1**

The entrance to the Flying Drunks' lair is well guarded. Four (4) Human Guards are near the entrance posted as sentries, while two (2) Human Bandits sit on stools at a table just inside the mouth of the cave. The Guards have strict orders to disallow entry to anyone who cannot show the Flying Drunk Symbol, or make the secret sign. If the PC's happen to have an item with the symbol, or have learned the secret sign, they may make a Charisma (Deception) check, DC 15, in order to gain entry. If the PC's go this route, each encounter with a Flying Drunk gang member will require another Charisma (Deception) check of DC 15, and require the presentation of the symbol, or making the gestures of the secret sign.

Unless the PC's took the Deception route at the first encounter, they will have to fight. If two (2) of the bandits fall dead, the other two will attempt to flee into the next room between Encounters 2 and 3.

This encounter includes one (1) Satyr and four (4) Human Bandits. This area is the main party room for the Flying Drunks. The main feature of the room is the large dining tables, which are very sturdy and well-built. The chairs surrounding these two tables are also intricately decorated and well-built, giving the impression that they may have belonged to a very wealthy person at one time.

The Satyr and the Bandits in this room are drinking, singing, and playing instruments. Although the Flying Drunks in this room are engaged in song and revelry, the room is too well-lit, and the tables too well placed, to allow the players to sneak by unnoticed.

**Encounter 5**

This encounter consists of six (6) **Human** Bandits and one (1) Wolf. In this encounter, you could have a couple different things occur. First, the bandits along with their wolf are simply moving toward the great hall, where Encounter 4 took place. The second option would be that these foes have discovered the PC's, and have set an ambush for them.

Area five (5) is another large opening where there are many stalagmites and stalactites, which can offer chances to hide. The dead-end passage near this area is a wine barrel storage room. There is no light at all in the storage room, nor **in** area five, other than what the PC's or Bandits brought with them. The description of this encounter will depend on which direction the PC's wish to go. It will also depend on how you want the foes to act, either aware or unaware of the characters' presence.

**Encounter 6**

This encounter consists of four (4) Giant Wolf Spiders. It is very dark in this portion of the

lair. If the PC's have light with them, or if they have darkvision, they can see a trail bypassing area number six. If they can see in this area, they also see that area six is full of spider webs.

The players can try to avoid this encounter by attempting a Dexterity (Stealth) check, versus each Giant Wolf Spider's Wisdom (Perception) checks. Basically, the DC for their Dexterity (Stealth) check is the highest of the four Wisdom (Perception) checks made by the Giant Wolf Spiders. If the PC's are carrying a light source, the Giant Wolf Spiders will make their checks with advantage.

**Encounter 7**

This encounter is simply a Trap and a Locked Door. Hopefully, the players will be cautious by this point. The Flying Drunks are not a gang to be taken lightly.

First, if the players attempt to open the door while it is locked, a fire trap located in the ceiling will be triggered. The Trap will do 5 (ldlO) damage to anyone within five feet of the door, on a failed Dexterity Save (DC 12). or half as much on a successful save.

This trap will also be triggered if the players attempt to bash down the door, or any other

method of opening the door, other than using the key or picking the lock successfully. The

triggering of the trap will alert the foes in area eight of the PC's presence.

The Trap can be triggered up to three (3) times.

The Locked Door can be opened with the key taken from Vanessa, the Yuan-ti Pureblood, or with a successful Dexterity (Sleight of Hand) check, DC 18.

>You move through another portion of the cave, full of natural rock formations. As you move out of the darkness, a few sconces along the walls give off dim light, allowing you to see.  Ahead of you is a large wooden door engraved with the Flying Drunks’ Symbol.

>You travel on, making a long, sweeping turn from North to East. A warm glow greets you from a room up ahead. Almost directly to your front, you see a large ogre seated on a blue, sturdy wooden crate. Beside him at a table are two bandits, who are tossing food to him, careful not to get too close.

**The Ogre Krowd**

The Ogre living in Kragnoroth's lair is known as Krowd. He is quite the legend among the Flying Drunks, even with their short history. The cave where the gang's lair is now was once only occupied by Krowd and the native spiders. The Flying Drunks came upon the cave, looking for a hideout after their major heist, not knowing of its current occupants. The Flying Drunks were there for a few days when a couple of the bandits came up missing. Kragnoroth soon figured out it was not the spiders who took his men, as the two others

before, who were still stuck in the webs, but it was Krowd. Through leaving gifts of food and drink, Kragnoroth eventually won the brute's favor. It was decided by some of the men that if Krowd was going to stay on with the gang, or rather, the gang would stay on with him, he should be initiated into the Flying Drunks. However, after two more bandits perished, and another was injured terribly, it was decided that an exception would be made for ogres.

**Surface Shaft**

This side area can offer your players some much needed rest, or a place to run to if things get bad. The Surface Shaft is about 50 feet tall. It is just wide enough for one medium sized creature at a time to climb a rope up it. At the top, the PC's will find themselves on a very tall hill, in a quite grove of trees.

>You move South out of the Ogre’s room through a dim cavern. The air is much fresher and easier to breathe here. The passage ahead splits, going right where many wine barrels are stacked, and straight forward, where you see more light coming from what could be another room.

**Encounter 13**

This encounter consists of four (4) Human Bandits, a Locked Door, and a Trap. The four Bandits are standing guard outside the room. Behind them is a section of stone wall with a heavy steel door set in it. Two torches hang on the wall, on either side of the steel door. The door is locked with a well-made lock, DC 18 to open it. Inside the room is the store room for

the entire Flying Drunks organization. Wine barrels line the Southern wall, while weapons, treasure chests, and food crates line the Eastern wall.

The trigger for the Trap is located five feet inside the store room. It is a pressure plate on the floor connected to an arrow trap. Tiny holes in the wall on the right, aimed at the entryway, are obscured by dust and cobwebs. The PC's may see them if they succeed on a Wisdom (Perception) check, DC 15. With a successful Intelligence (Investigation) check, DC 15, the PC's can discover the pressure plate. The trap activates when more than 20 pounds of weight is placed on the pressure plate, releasing four (4) arrows. Each arrow makes a ranged attack with a +8 bonus against a random target within 10 feet of the pressure plate. (If there are no targets in the area, the arrows simply strike the opposite wall.) A target that is hit takes 3 (ld6) piercing damage.

Use Individual Treasure Table 3 for the foes in this encounter. There are also three chests in the store room: one is full of trail rations, another is full of water skins full of drinkable water, and the third is full of treasure (roll on Hoard Treasure Table to determine loot).

wine, Kragnoroth's personal treasure hoard, a weapon rack, a bedroll, and a table with

Table 3, and Kragnoroth's chest contains 200 GP, plus roll on Hoard Treasure Table.

**RESOLUTION**

Although this is where the printed material ends, this does not have to be the end of the

adventure. The cave does not have to end in Encounter 15, but can proceed downward

into the underdark, opening up other possibilities for adventure. Remember to reward the characters for their work, based on the hook used from the beginning. This does not have to spell the end for the Flying Drunks, nor even for Kragnoroth the Drunk himself, if you so wish. Maybe Kragnoroth gets away in the end, and the players have to pursue him and his gang through many other adventures yet to come.

**Appendix B:**

**Background**

**Options**

**BOUNTY HUNTER**

**BACKGROUND**

You spend your life hunting down and capturing or killing wanted criminals and monsters. You are part investigator, part hunter, and you know your way into and out of almost any situation. The best part of being a bounty hunter, however, is the cash payment, and you are very good at knowing how to get paid for your services.

**Skill Proficiencies:** Investigation, Perception

**Tool Proficiency:** Disguise kit

**Languages:** Any two of your choice

**Equipment:** 50' silk rope, lock, hunting trap, traveler's clothes, and a pouch with 10 gold pieces in it.

  

**FEATURE: GETTING PAID**

Whenever a wanted criminal is killed or captured by you or your allies, you receive a bonus payment equal to 1 gold piece per Experience Point of the wanted criminal or criminals. The time needed to receive the payment, and from whom the payment comes, is up to your DM. Also, membership in the Rusty Shackles (Appendix C), is recommended for characters with this background.

**SUGGESTED CHARACTERISTICS**

Bounty hunters can be a rough lot. Much of their life is spent on the road, chasing down dangerous criminals and monsters. Such a life makes casual social interactions very difficult for the bounty hunter. Cash payment is a top priority, and the glitter of gold always seems to make the day go better.

**d8 Personality**

1 There is nothing I like more than a good mystery.

2 I have a dark sense of humor.

3 Every criminal needs to be taught a lesson, and I am the teacher.

4 If it’s worth the gold, I will capture or kill it.

5 Every bounty is worth pursuing.

6 I’m well-known in my home town, now I want to be world famous.

7 I love a good insult, especially when I’m the one dishing them out.

8 It’s a nasty job, but someone has to do it.

**d6 Ideal**

1 Greed: I will do whatever it takes to become wealthy. (evil)

2 Aspiration: I work hard to be the best there is at my craft. (any)

3 Fairness: A fair wage for fair work. (lawful)

4 Greater Good: Our lot is to sacrifice our lives in defense of others. (good)

5 Independence: Not every criminal is evil, and not every bounty is just. (chaotic)

6 Sincerity: I am what I was born to be. (neutral)

**d6 Bond**

1 I will get revenge on the criminal gang that destroyed my life.

2 I have a family, but I have no idea where they are. One day, I hope to see them again.

3 Somewhere out there, I have a child who doesn’t know me. I’m making the world better for him or her.

4 I was once a wanted criminal who turned in my accomplices for a reward.

5 Thugs murdered my boss, stole all my possessions, and left me to die. Vengeance will be mine.

6 I’ll always remember my first bounty hunt.

**d6 Flaw**

1 I can’t say “No” to a pretty face.

2 I’ll say just about anything.

3 My pride will probably lead to my destruction.

4 All the information I get, I keep secret.

5 Violence is the answer to almost every question.

6 Careful? Be careful? Pffft!

**ADVENTURE SPECIFIC BOND**

**d8 Bond**

1 I work for Ship Suljack in Luskan, and I have been sent after Kragnoroth the Drunk.

2 I was robbed by the Flying Drunks and I want payback.

3 My girlfriend Vanessa left me for Kragnoroth the Drunk.

4 I was a member of the Flying Drunks, but I didn’t get my fair cut on a robbery, so I’m going to get what belongs to me.

5 Kragnoroth and his gang owe my tavern a lot of money, and I’m going to get it, one way or

another.

6 My friend was tricked by Kragnoroth the Drunk into becoming a criminal. I have to rescue him.

7 The ogre in that cave will pay for his evil crimes.

8 Nobody operates a criminal gang in my neck of the woods. Nobody.

**Appendix C: The**

**Rusty Shackles**

**Organization**

The Rusty Shackles is a network of bounty hunters, informants, and officers of the law who make it their priority to remove criminals and monsters from society. The organization is relatively new compared to other organizations, but it is well-manned, and well-funded. The Rusty Shackles often operate as lone agents throughout the Forgotten Realms, but may

seek out the help of others for particularly tough assignments. The Rusty Shackles ideology is somewhat noble, even though its agents rarely are.

**_Motto:_** "Wanted: Dead or Alive. To protect and collect."

**_Beliefs:_** The Rusty Shackles beliefs can be summarized as follows: The world is dangerous enough without criminals and monsters wandering around in it. Every crime, and every criminal, has a price to pay. Information is money.

**_Goals:_** Rid the world of wanted criminals and monsters, amass wealth, gain power and influence, and thereby make the world safer.

**_Typical guests:_** Typical Rusty Shackles quests include hunting down wanted criminals, killing violent monsters, assisting local law officers, acting as undercover agents, and investigating crime.
